page.layout: One text column, centre of the page, with a marginal note at the lower right. Above the column: running head, left. Printed page number 75 at the upper right. Left of the frame: edge of the neighbouring page, not transcribed.

main_text.p: qui & contra Barbaros in militia Romana, egregiam nauauit operam, & aduersus Iudæos agebat Magistrum Equitum, cùm Traianus ipse ductor esset; & postea sub Adriano Martyrio coronatus. Quinimò, exercitum lustrans Traianus, inuentos vndecim mille Christianos, diis sacra facere recusantes, in Armeniam relegauit, vt ignominiæ notati Christiani esse desinerent. Cùm vero Romulus Imperatoris domui præpositus eum admoneret, vt de re minus prudenter gesta: professus se quoque Christianum, eius iussu verberibus cæsus obtruncatur. Quid interim moliuntur Clemens & Anacletus Romani Episcopi? num hos milites & duces in iugulum Imperatoris armant? certè fecissent Iulius secundus, Pius quintus, Gregorius 1 3. Nihil minus. Sed ipsi suos iugulos & ceruices securi præbent, & vna cum his illa clarissima Ecclesiæ lumina, tanquam tot in caliginosa nocte scintillantia sydera, {p}SimeonEuseb. lib.3.ca.26. frater Domini, Episcopus Hierosolymitanis, annos natus centum & viginti, Onesimus Ephesinus, & Ignatius Antiochenus, qui etiam

page.notes: The printed page number 75 and running head "LIB. II. Scutum Regium." are read as printed; the head's number is not repeated in the running head text. The reference mark before "Simeon" is a small letter p, matched to the margin note. Doubtful: "Euseb." (the long s is read as plain s), and "lib.3.ca.26." (read as printed). "Gregorius 1 3." keeps the printed space between 1 and 3. The mark before "Antiochenus" is an ornament-like glyph that I could not identify, so I have left it out. The left edge fragment is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Ends with the catchword "etiam" below the last full line.
